observation_summary: The StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence) method incorrectly relied on the CharSequence.equals() contract, which is undefined for different implementations of CharSequence. This caused equality checks to fail for objects that represent the same character sequence but are of different types (e.g., String vs. StringBuilder).
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces the reliance on the unreliable CharSequence.equals() method with a robust character-by-character comparison using CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches(). This is a change to the computational strategy (the algorithm) used to determine equality, as the original method was fundamentally flawed for the CharSequence interface contract.
evidence_used: The bug report states that CharSequence.equals() has undefined behavior for different implementations.
The fix_diff_oracle shows the removal of the direct cs1.equals(cs2) call and the introduction of a character-by-character comparison using CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches().
The failing test case confirms that StringUtils.equals() failed when comparing a String with a StringBuilder, which are different implementations of CharSequence.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the issue involves the CharSequence interface, the fix is not about changing the signature or the communication contract between components, but rather implementing a correct internal algorithm to handle the equality logic for the interface.
The fix adds a check for String instances, but the core of the fix is the replacement of the equality algorithm, not just adding a guard.
